It's incredibly difficult to figure out how to structure my side chats here. As you can see, I've already got quite a number in the pinned section, and you know there's a few of them: avatar image generation, video generation, repo wiki, brain sync. Those I know I'm definitely using. How do you think I should structure?
[image:image/jpeg workspace/user/media_library/image/f9/f9238367e2923663e86f60a3704bb3b1bb4eeb1a5d6581f287129de5b1d9748d.jpg]

You've already got the right instinct — 1 chat = 1 workstream. I'd just make the tiers mean something:

- `• SYSTEM` — about Muse itself, nothing else
- `• REPO: X` — code homes (WIKIBRAIN, RAWLOGS, FACIAL-ANALYSIS)
- `• MAKE: X` — creation (IMAGE, VIDEO, AVATAR, FACE-BOOK)
- `• FLOW: X` — things that run on schedule (SYNC, STYLOMETRY, MUSIC, WIKI PHOTO)

Rules I'd use: main = triage/inbox, nothing lives there. Pinned = has an active cron, goal, or artifact. No cron/goal = archive, don't delete.

That'd drop you to ~11 pinned and the `•/••/•••` soup goes away. Your four you named stay exactly where they are.

Want me to rename/archive them into that shape?

Is there some kind of testing instrument you can give me that will help us establish baseline, etc
Build's running in the background now. I'll hand it over the moment it's done — open it on your phone, run it cold first thing tomorrow morning for your sober baseline, then again around events.
OH I have an awesome idea
Let's hear it.
So that we can add images without any tos concerns i want you to still keep posting images to entries hur if they have nudity they should have it blur/pixelate/censor

Love it. Simple version: at media intake I look at every image, and anything nude gets a blurred/pixelated derivative embedded instead of the raw file. Registry notes which ones are censored.

One honest limit: there's no reliable auto-detector in the pipeline, so it's my eyeballs at intake, not an algorithm. I'll catch the obvious stuff; anything borderline I'll flag rather than guess.

Want me to sweep the ~40 images already embedded and censor any nudity retroactively?
Yes

The battery's done. ~4 minutes: vitals check-in, reaction time, digit span, Stroop, finger tap, typing burst. Runs stay on your device, and it builds your baseline from sober morning runs — comparisons kick in after three.
Testing instrument

Run it cold first thing in the morning a few days straight, then around events. Paste the results block here each time and I'll log it against the labels — that's what turns "I feel off" into a measurable delta.

Done. Swept all 39 embedded images — only one had actual nudity: the jaredtricia keepsake photo. It's pixelated now, caption says so, and it's merged.

The rule's standing policy from here on: every image gets eyeballed at intake, nudity gets pixelated before it touches the repo.
I mean specifically through my writing. Something that gives me a small writing prompt or instruction custom built and optimized to identify markers

Say less — writing-specific instrument, here it is:

**The 6-minute sample.** Same three prompts every run. Fixed prompts mean topic can't confound the signal — all variance is you. One sitting, no editing, no backspacing.

W1 — STREAM, 3 min: write nonstop about the last 2 hours. Don't stop. Stall? Retype your last sentence until new words come.

W2 — ROOM, 90 sec: describe the room you're in, in as much detail as you can, like I've never seen it.

W3 — ARGUE, 90 sec: hot dog — sandwich or not? Argue it in 5+ sentences.

Paste all three here labeled W1/W2/W3 with the time. I run them through the extractor and score against baseline; repeats build a separate instrument baseline. W1 hunts your length markers, W2 is the topic-fixed control, W3 stresses reasoning structure. Adding typo density to the extractor too — the no-edit rule makes it measurable for the first time.

Do one right now. You're ~15 min post-onset — perfect labeled sample.

Want a timer page that enforces the clock and the no-backspace rule?
